--- Page 1 (Beckerman_23a) --- Dear Jack, We're a little late in answering your letter of May 14 - which we received a few days ago. All the contents were enjoyed as much as the letter itself. From the 'Old Friends Directory' we learned that you're the only Bront representative in the place. But 'Account Current' testifies that the rotation system won't be the means of seeing the home town once again. Well, with the way the news is going now, perhaps that 30 month minimum will be unnecessary. You write that things are a little too comfortable right now. He can see what you mean - like the time when you were in the states & wanting to get going - even overseas to change the routine. Perhaps this time too, you'll have the opportunity to get out of that comfort zone before acquiring any 'native' status. And visualizing that you do - we wonder if milkman, maid service etc. won't be missed. It's always easier to adapt yourself to them than break away - but we're very sure that whichever type war you fight - it'll be with your best. Those fotos of the office certainly give us to see with a room efficient organize [illegible] --- Page 2 (Beckerman_23b) --- covered. A place like that must be a veritable behive when in action - with all the machines buzzing away, and every zero to be accounted for. All things here are on a rather different plane but all's all right its way! Sarah was over last week to invite us to the Seder, but as both fell on weekdays Papa thought it wouldn't be too convenient; but we couldn't get away without making our annual trip to the phones of Bklyn that easily. He compromised and I ended by attending Seder #2 and Mama & Papa making the trip the following Sat. in time to eat "famed Chupnick special "chint" (translated that equals a 5' by 5' pot of potatoes that has steamed through 24 hrs. of cooking). The Seder contained the usual satisfying elements of a delicious meal; before and after which Mishloach Maseed through the whole 'mighile' with just the right intonations and 'jazzing up' of which he is the connoisseur but under Sarah's watchful eye not being able to even accidentally turn two pages at once.... He reminisced about that time when there were 17 people at the table instead of just 7 - ended up with a toast to more scenes like that in the near future. "Abcato" once we has been scarce mail of & his last letter tells us --- Page 3 (Beckerman_23c) --- of moving forward once again - the still on the same island.... Papa working and tells us of the notice posted at Bendel's - "you need not report to work the day the fall of Germany is announced" - That will be cause for celebration, and it doesn't seem far off now..... Today is Easter Sunday, and as usual we are not spending it walking up Fifth Avenue", - but rather up Bront Park where the perfume is not artificial..... Just in case the enclosed slip of paper had any importance attached to it - we're enclosing it. You probably slipped it into the letter accidentally. Also sending along separately the City College Alumni Reporter which arrived here yester day..... We were very pleasantly surprised to find a letter from Deshie in the mail. It seems as if he waited until he had some good news to write us, for it does seem as if he's gotten a break in the way of a pretty interesting job and no longer is a "blind puppet"..... Mama has the good intentions of writing you herself and "says" positively in the next letter". Until then we'll sign off with Love & Regards, Mama Papa Suite
